messages:
Sara C.: Ok team — AcmeCorp POC just moved to pricing approval. They want committed capacity for production: sustained ~50 req/s (text-gen, 1k context) with short spikes to ~200 req/s for <5m. HIPAA + customer-managed KMS. Need: recommended reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, preheat plan, and an estimate of committed cost vs burst credits. @Nate O. can you start?
Nate O.: quick one: which model family are they testing in POC? that changes GPU counts a lot.
Sara C.: They tested with rwd-13b-q4_0 and with a 2x batch setup earlier. latency SLO is 500ms p95.
Priya R.: ok — rough mapping from our perf sheets: for rwd-13b-q4_0 at 1k context, one A10-like slot ~12 req/s sustained@500ms if batching 2-4. For 50 req/s sustained we'll need baseline 4 slots. for 200 req/s peak we need additional 3-4 slots for short bursts. so reserved baseline=4, burst pool=3, max=7.
Tom B.: +1 to Priya's calc. also depends on KV cache hit rate. if they warm prefix cache to ~80% we can reduce burst need by ~1 slot. recommend we bake a cache-warmup run in the preheat window.
Priya R.: autoscale proposal: min=4 (reserved), max=7, scale_step=1, cooldown=60s, policy=step. prewarm recipe: run these 10 representative prompts (we have them from the POC) in a 30-min preheat to populate KV and compiled kernels.
Priya R.: CLI for devops: ```
rwctl pool update --name acme-prod --min 4 --max 7 --scale-step 1 --cooldown 60
rwctl preheat run --pool acme-prod --prompts-file acme_prefixes.json --duration 30m
```
Nate O.: pricing questions from finance: what is delta reserved vs on-demand for that footprint? and how are burst credits priced if they exceed reserved pool?
Tom B.: ballpark: reserved baseline (4 slots A100-40 equiv) = $XXXk/month + support. burst credits are cheaper than sustained on-demand but still priced per-GPU-hour; short bursts (under 10h/mo) usually cost less than the delta vs reserved. I'll pull exact numbers for the quote.
Liam O.: security flags: AcmeCorp wants customer-managed keys + monthly rotation, audit logs exported to their SIEM, and proof of SOC2 control. Dedicated pool with VPC peering or private deployment is the recommended path. audit logs and KMS integration available on Dedicated and Private.
Sara C.: do we need any special wording in the security questionnaire to show the fallback plan? they asked about fail open vs fail closed for KMS.
Liam O.: we should state: "By default, keys are required for model I/O at rest; we support KMS with rotation and will not fallback to plaintext. In a rare KMS outage we can route to a pre-approved rotate-key but that requires a signed runbook." short answer: fail-closed by default, failover via an approved rotated key only.
Nate O.: ops question from customer: during bursts, will autoscale preempt lower-priority tenants? how do we guarantee noisiness isolation?
Priya R.: for Dedicated pools we isolate the reservation. For Hosted we do capacity hedging: route-by-policy, preferring reserved vhosts. We can also provide an opt-in isolated pool for Acme so noisy neighbors won't impact them.
Tom B.: fallback strategy if we hit max capacity: 1) route to quantized smaller model (rwd-7b-q4) 2) increase per-token latency tolerance to 800ms p95 for non-critical routes 3) shed non-essential endpoints. We document these in the runbook.
Sara C.: timeline: customer wants committed pricing + contract language by EOW. can we get Priya/Tom numbers and Liam security blurb by Thursday?
Priya R.: yes, I'll run a quick bench with the exact batch parameters Monday and update numbers Wed.
Tom B.: I'll extract cost delta and burst-credit example by Wed.
Liam O.: I'll draft the KMS + audit answers and a short runbook snippet by Wed afternoon.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: preheat-job for acme-prod queued for 2023-11-06T09:00:00Z (simulated). :robot_face:
Sara C.: great — I'll assemble the questionnaire answers and the SLA text and loop in legal. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
Nate O.: one last note — add a canary rollout: start with 10% traffic for 24h then 50% for 6h before full cutover. small ask but avoids surprises.
Priya R.: noted. canary policy: 10% -> 50% -> 100%, rollback if p95 > 1s or error rate > 1%.
Sara C.: perfect. locking this thread for action items. will follow up with a consolidated doc and quote. :white_check_mark:
